stage: independent initial inspection before editor proposals
sourceObservations: N/S read as tall, largely blank blue slabs. The crown-to-front transition makes a broad horizontal tonal boundary. The few small rectangular facets appear attached to an otherwise unarticulated surface.
E/W show the broad top and end surfaces. The bottom becomes a nearly black unstructured band; W includes a thin dark horizontal finished-end stripe. That stripe is not convincing stone construction.

The actual source collection is S33_PROP_rock-wall-edge.001, with six mesh objects under an identity root. Full-width continuous crag carries both exact X=±0.5 eight-point profiles. The actual root metadata and source asset record both declare W and E ports.

Native +X has finished_end_strata centered near X=.505 with an outer extent near .511; its decorative protrusion conflicts with treating the declared E plane as a flush connector. This weak original part/protrusion is not a locked design constraint. E-end character may be rebuilt inside the exact connector envelope. Native +X is most directly visible in the W published facing.

After enabling the hidden source collection for evaluated transforms, actual total bounds are min[-.5,-.510999978,0], max[.510999978,.510999978,1.163219094]. The original functional body is a full-cell base; attached relief explains the small outside bounds.

The library saves an incidental active presentation camera with a different elevation. It has no camera matching the registered source-camera record. The source-camera record and approved native middle agree on the actual publication contract, so the incidental active camera must not replace registration.
fixedTargetObservations: The fixed target offers broad, irregular, softly worn cobalt stones with substantial turning planes, luminous cyan upper surfaces, restrained deep crevices and rounded purposeful small stones.

Useful targets are readable stone volume, more deliberate construction, softer highlights and lower-surface information. Copying every white highlight ribbon, pebble or swelling is unnecessary; the target is a single S-view design reference, not evidence for exact profiles, joins or unseen facings.
The target has a much more varied face than the source. Native changes should be materially visible at logical size, not merely small texture noise or extra parts.
approvedFamilyObservations: All eight supplied family dependency hashes independently match the brief. I opened the actual approved project and inspected its geometry, root, camera, material nodes and symmetric SUN rig, as well as all four published frames.

The approved middle uses broad carved stone cells, cyan upper planes, deeper cobalt lower surfaces and quieter highlights than the target. It establishes shared native connector color/normal and capture/material continuity, without certifying the future edge candidate.

The actual approved middle has identity root; full-cell X=±.5 connector cuts; one native material with vertex albedo; roughness≈.88, specular IOR≈.12 and emission≈.38; overhead SUN 1.35 and equal four cardinal SUN fills≈.42 with shadows disabled. Shared endpoint Y/Z and albedo pair exactly in the native asset. Full actual measurements are retained in initial-source-audit.json.
scoresExplanation: Comparative observations of this original only; no numerical approval threshold or score for the sibling asset is implied.
recommendedPriorities: Replace broad blank planes and rectangular attached facets with coherent worn stone volume and deliberate large-scale construction that reads in all four facings.
Preserve cobalt family continuity while making lower surfaces and soft facet highlights readable; remove black dead bands and thin artificial strata artifacts.

Retain both declared connectors and match the approved native middle at each shared position/profile/color/normal. Prove both joins in independently assembled current browser captures at logical, phone and fractional scale/phase.
